MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MAY 7, 2018

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
CHAIRMAN MEDAWAR.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  COMMISSIONER EDLER led the assembly in the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Chair Medawar, Zigrang, Carman, Edler, Schachter,
  Scott, Yoo

  Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Sr. Planner Naughton

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING OF
  MARCH 5, 2018.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  None

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A. WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL RESOLUTIONS THAT ARE PRESENTED FOR THE
  CONSIDERATION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION ON TONIGHT’S AGENDA AND
  ALL SUCH RESOLUTIONS SHALL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6-A.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A. COMMISSIONER IPADS DISTRIBUTION AND TRAINING (Training Session by
  Administrative Services Director)

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a brief training on city assigned
  iPads and how to access agendas via iLegislate.

  Tom Pulls, Out of the Box I.T., provided additional information and training.

  B. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 19-15; APPLICANT: TOLL BROTHERS; LOCATION:
  THE RESIDENCES AT ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB; A request to amend PA-19-
  15, to approve the architectural styles for 31 proposed homes in The Residences at the
  Rolling Hills Country Club development.

  Sr. Planner Naughton provided the Planning Commission with background on this project
  and a summary of the staff report for Planning Application No. 19-15 (PA-19-15).

  Sr. Planner Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission discuss
  this item and approve the amendment to PA-19-15, incorporating the proposed
  architectural design for Product B homes into the overall architectural design of The
  Residences at Rolling Hills Country Club.

  Chuck Lande, Master Developer and Builder, Chadmar Group, stated that Toll Brothers

  1
Planning Commission Minutes
May 7, 2018
   has been brought in to do 31 lots to add to the diversity of the neighborhood and stated
  that they have approved the new designs.

  Peter Hemphill, Toll Brothers, stated that their sales gallery will open on May 19th and a
  website is available with more details on the project.

  Bob Hidey, Robert Hidey Architects, provided the Planning Commission with a PowerPoint
  presentation with an overview of the project location and details on the exterior and interior
  design, architectural styles, and materials which will be used on the homes.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT expressed his concern in regards to the site plan showing
  identical homes in close proximity to each other. Mr. Hidey clarified that each of the homes
  shown are designed with a different elevation. Planning Director Wahba stated that there
  is an intent not to have similar homes next to each other and added that the master
  developer and Toll Brothers will make sure of this.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT expressed his opposition to the designs titles, 3B, 1C, and 4C.
  Specifically, the lack of overhangs, roofs that don’t meet the top of the wall, repetitive
  features on the front, and stated that these designs are unlike anything found in the city.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that three out of four of the designs do not meet
  Neighborhood Compatibility nor aesthetics and stated that they do not belong in the city.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG expressed his disagreement and stated that the designs are
  historically correct. As this may not be what is typically seen in the city, the designs are
  well done and believes that this area holds its own as a new development.

  Bob Hidey, Robert Hidey Architects, stated that he believes that the designs are consistent
  with the guidelines and although opinions may differ, he can point to the details and how
  the styles are defined and consistent with those styles.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT expressed his opposition to the designs as presented and
  stated that they are grossly out of character.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that this is a departure of what has been done in the city,
  but this is a new development contained in its own neighborhood. Planning Director
  Wahba stated that in the context of the general design parameters, these designs work.
  When you apply Neighborhood Compatibility, you would compare it to what is there.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that these homes do not look like anything that would
  be approved and stated that Mr. Hidey did a good job with the designs in 2015, but the
  proposed design do not meet Neighborhood Compatibility.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that if design 4C which is a modern farmhouse was
  being proposed for Dapplegray or Strawberry Lanes neighborhood, then he would agree
  that they are too modern. However, in this subdivision, the designs work. Also, when
  vegetation grows in, it will soften the look.

  CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that the European Farmhouse design does not look like the
  ranch style that is typical, however, having it in this specific development he understands
  how the architects and designers can implement these designs. CHAIR MEDAWAR asked
  about the homes with only two-car garages and the lack of space to park a golf cart.

  Mr. Hidey stated that their design team takes criteria from the clients and there was
  discussion early in the project in defining distinct plans in order for the variety of plans to
  target specific users with the result of attracting a series of buyers.

  Sr. Planner Naughton stated that in the 2015 approval, Product C homes have either a
  two or three car-garage with an additional one-car garage, which would accommodate a
  golf cart. The Toll Brothers’ Product B designs have the same type of configuration.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about the distinction between one of the designs
  in 2015 to the proposed design. COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that in his opinion they
  are substantially different.

  COMMISSIONER EDLER inquired about resolution to the issue with some of the homes
  being outside of the boundaries of the PVP School District.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that she is unsure that these are compatible with the
  ambience of the city and expressed her opposition for the materials being used.
  CHAIR MEDAWAR asked staff if this project meets the city’s guidelines. Planning Director

  2
Planning Commission Minutes
May 7, 2018
   Wahba stated that the proposed designs are different and direction from City Council was
  to make the designs rural or ranch-style. These designs are an improvement from what
  was initially presented and are more consistent with the designs approved in 2015.

  CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that he must keep an open mind since this is not the typical
  ranch style in the city, however, this architecture caters to a new clientele.

  COMMISSIONER YOO commented that other applicants were directed to maintain a
  ranch style and a “wedding cake” effect in their design and is unsure how far applicants,
  even in new developments, should be allowed to defer from that. Planning Director Wahba
  stated that it is at the discretion of the Planning Commissioners’ to have the architect
  respond to their suggestions.

  Mr. Hidey stated that one way to consider this project is that it is designed as an overall
  community and further explained that there is a balance with first and second story
  occupancy.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT commented that the homes are not ranch style. CHAIR
  MEDAWAR concurred but stated that he is willing to accept some of the designs
  considering that this is a planned community and asked if this is a gated community. Mr.
  Hidey answered that he is not certain, but believes it is a restricted community. Planning
  Director Wahba stated that the City Council is discussing the issue of this being a gated
  community in closed session and will eventually be discussed in open session.

  A discussion ensued in regards to specific designs and specific features within the
  designs.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN expressed her concern with what is allowed in planned
  developments and stated that they should still reflect the characteristics of the community.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Mr. Hemphill stated that
  designs 1C and 4C seem to be of the most concern but requested that he would prefer
  that the acceptable designs be approved. Getting no approval would put their sales
  program on hold. The designs that are not approved would be reevaluated, and may be
  redesigned and presented as a package for separate approval.

  The Planning Commission agreed to take a vote on the individual designs.

  •  Design 1A (7-Yes / 0-No)
  •  Design 1B (7-Yes / 0-No)
  •  Design 1C (2-Yes / 5-No)
  The PLANNING COMMISSIONERS provided suggestions for improvement.
  •  Design 2A (7-Yes / 0-No)
  •  Design 2B (6-Yes / 1-No)
  •  Design 2C (4-Yes / 3-No)
  •  Design 3A (7-Yes / 0-No)
  •  Design 3B (4-Yes / 3-No)
  •  Design 3C (3-Yes / 4-No)
  The PLANNING COMMISSIONERS provided suggestions for improvement.
  •  Design 4A (6-Yes / 1-No)
  •  Design 4B (5-Yes / 2-No)
  •  Design 4C (3-Yes / 4-No)

  9 out of the 12 designs have been approved.

  A discussion ensued about how this will affect where the homes are placed.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,
  APPROVE THE AMENDMENT TO PA-19-15 APPROVING THE 31 HOMES IN THE 9
  DESIGNS AS APPROVED BY THE PLANNING COMMISSION AND EXCLUDING
  DESIGNS 1-C, 3-C, AND 4C AND TO HAVE THE THREE REVISED DESIGNS COME
  BACK TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION FOR APPROVAL.

  Ayes: CHAIR MEDAWAR, ZIGRANG, CARMAN, EDLER, SCHACHTER, SCOTT, YOO
  Noes:
  Absent:
  Abstain:

  Planning Director Wahba stated that there is a 20 day appeal period for this item.

  3
Planning Commission Minutes
May 7, 2018
 8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 05-18; APPLICANT: CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; A resolution recommending to the City Council
  approval of an ordinance amending and restating chapter 17.56 of the RHEMC, related to
  accessory dwelling units.

  Planning Director Wahba provided the Planning Commission with a summary of the staff
  report for PA-05-18.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission
  open the public hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing,
  and approved resolution 05-18, recommending to the City Council, approval of an
  ordinance amending and restating Chapter 17.56 of the RHEMC, related to accessory
  dwelling units.

  VICE CHAIR ZIGRANG moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked if street parking will now be allowed. Planning
  Director Wahba responded by saying that although parking is not really an issue in the
  city, if there is a need for street parking, the city will need to approve a permit.

  COMMISSIONER EDLER inquired about filing who will be occupying an ADU. Planning
  Director Wahba stated that a covenant is required for ADU’s, which states that one unit
  must be owner-occupied and cannot be sold separately from the main residence. There
  is a new requirement regarding occupancy filing, however, staff will need to develop the
  details on the filing process.

  In response to a questions from COMMISSIONER SCOTT regarding section no.
  17.56.070 (d), Planning Director Wahba stated that he will speak to the city attorney
  regarding the wording which requires that one of the units be owner occupied and what
  would happen to the ADU (in terms of its legality) if the owner moves out.

  VICE CHAIR SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

  VICE CHAIR ZIGRANG moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE PA-05-18, A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVING AN
  ORDINANCE AMENDING AND RESTATING CHAPTER 17.56 OF THE RHEMC
  SUBJECT TO THE REVISION AS STATED BY THE PLANNING COMMISSION.

  Ayes: CHAIR MEDAWAR, ZIGRANG, CARMAN, EDLER, SCHACHTER, SCOTT, YOO
  Noes:
  Absent:
  Abstain:

9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  None

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

  Planning Director Wahba reminded the Planning Commissioners who have not completed
  their Form 700s to complete and return them to the City Clerk.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that now that the iPads are available, hard copies of
  agenda packets will be discontinued.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT requested to continue receiving hard copies, specifically of
  large format plans.

  4
Planning Commission Minutes
May 7, 2018
 11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A. PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, MARCH 19, 2018.

  B. DRAFT MINUTES OF THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING, APRIL 16,
  2018.

  C. CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, MARCH 27, 2018.

  D. CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, APRIL 10, 2018.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCOTT to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11-A THROUGH 11-D.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR MEDAWAR adjourned the meeting at 9:07 p.m.
